selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: After reflecting on one spring, what conclusion did the traveler reach about people who reject resurrection?
questions.answer: He concluded that punishment in Hell would be fully just for them.

questions.question: What mistake does the passage say is involved in denying resurrection?
questions.answer: It means rejecting many divine promises and denying the power of Allah to bring people back.

questions.question: How is Allah described in relation to His promise of resurrection?
questions.answer: He is presented as absolutely powerful and irresistible, and as One whose majesty includes rightful anger against denial.

questions.question: Through whom has the promise of resurrection been repeatedly conveyed?
questions.answer: It has been conveyed through all the prophets.

questions.question: How often does the passage say this promise has been stated in the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It says the promise appears many times, both directly and indirectly, in thousands of verses.

questions.question: What comparison is made to help explain the possibility of resurrection?
questions.answer: The final gathering is compared with the many revivals seen every spring, which are described as even more amazing in some ways.

questions.question: According to the passage, how difficult is resurrection for Allah compared with the springtime renewals?
questions.answer: It is easier for Him than those repeated spring renewals.

questions.question: What does the traveler’s inner self say in response to this reflection?
questions.answer: It affirms the truth of what was said and accepts it in belief.

questions.question: What main belief is being defended in this passage?
questions.answer: The belief that resurrection and the final gathering will truly happen.

questions.question: What sign from the natural world leads the traveler to this belief?
questions.answer: Seeing the realities displayed in a single spring leads him to it.

questions.question: Why does denying resurrection count as more than a simple intellectual mistake in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it is treated as a rejection of Allah’s repeated promises and of His unlimited power.

questions.question: What does the repeated mention of prophets and Qur’anic verses show?
questions.answer: It shows that the promise of resurrection is strongly established through revelation and is not a minor teaching.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about Allah’s ability by calling resurrection easier than spring revivals?
questions.answer: It suggests that such a task is effortless for Him and fully within His power.

questions.question: Why is spring used as an argument for resurrection?
questions.answer: Because spring shows countless forms of life being brought forth again in an ordered and remarkable way.

questions.question: What moral idea connects disbelief and punishment in this passage?
questions.answer: The idea is that when someone knowingly rejects clear truth and divine promise, punishment becomes just.

questions.question: How does the ending strengthen the argument emotionally and spiritually?
questions.answer: The inner self does not resist in the end but yields and confirms belief.

questions.question: What does the traveler understand after considering only one spring?
questions.answer: He understands that resurrection is real and that denying it is a grave error.

questions.question: What does the passage connect denial of resurrection with besides disbelief itself?
questions.answer: It connects it with denying Allah’s promises and His power.

questions.question: Which two sources of testimony for resurrection are named in the passage?
questions.answer: The prophets and the verses of the Qur’an.

questions.question: In what two ways does the passage say the Qur’an points to resurrection?
questions.answer: It points to it openly and also through indirect indications.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that the promises were given many times?
questions.answer: To show that the message is firm, repeated, and beyond excuse for those who reject it.

questions.question: What is implied about the scale of spring by calling its gatherings miraculous?
questions.answer: It implies that spring contains vast and wondrous restorations of life that point to Allah’s creative power.

questions.question: If spring contains many repeated restorations of life, what inference does the traveler draw about the final resurrection?
questions.answer: He infers that the final resurrection is certainly possible and even easier for Allah.

questions.question: What is the significance of the nafs saying that it believes?
questions.answer: It shows that the argument has reached the person’s inner self and won its acceptance.
